ai.title: Add subscriber access tier row helper
ai.summary: New `subscriber-access-tiers.ts` exports `subscriberAccessTierRows` to format access tier counts. Maps 'full', 'limited', 'unknown' to localized labels with `toLocaleString('en-US')`. Falls back to em-dash for undefined counts. Scope: `common/src/util/`.

eli5.text: If you look at a summary of how many subscribers have each kind of access tier (full, limited, or not yet sorted), the numbers will now appear as properly formatted counts (like 1,234 instead of 1234), and any tier with no data will show a dash instead of blank space. This only affects the internal tools staff use to inspect subscriber tier breakdowns, not anything you would see as a customer today.

ai.summary: Added 2026-09-14T03:46:00Z entry to SOLAR_PRICE_CHANGES for FREEBUFF_SOLAR_PRO_4_MODEL_ID, raising price from 5 to 10. Marked SOLAR_REGULAR_OFFER as historical; solarOfferAt() resolves current pricing. Updated common/src/constants/freebuff-solar-promo.ts.

eli5.text: The Solar Pro 4 limited-time trial now costs 10 instead of 5, as of 3:46 AM UTC on September 14, 2026. Anyone buying that trial pays double what it cost the day before, while the 'Limited-time trial' label stays exactly the same. The new price was scheduled in advance: the app checks the current time against a list of planned price changes and shows whichever one applies, so the increase switched on by itself at the appointed minute with no new release needed.

entries.title: Agent Runtime update: compact-history

ai.title: Agent runtime reserves space for system, tools and step prompt before
ai.summary: A new `fitToolResults` helper in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/fit-tool-results.ts` clips fresh `read_files` contents and oversized JSON tool results so the latest tool calls and their results fit the remaining token budget after older history has been compacted. The runtime now passes a `fixedTokenCount` into `maybeCompactHistory` (system prompt, tool schemas and the step prompt plus its scaffolding), so the context budget is sized against the live request overhead rather than only against summary text. `compactRequestHistory` preserves the newest historical entries that fit the actual remainder, keeps steering prompts together, and reserves a legacy request as historical memory when the current prompt is absent.
ai.evidence: New file `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/fit-tool-results.ts` exports `fitToolResults`, called from `compactRequestHistory` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/compact-history.ts` (which itself is invoked by `maybeCompactHistory` after the new `fixedTokenCount` parameter is threaded through). The `loopAgentSteps` call site in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` now passes `fixedTokenCount` composed of `countTokens(system) + countTokensJson(toolsForTokenCount) + (stepPrompt ? ... : 0)`.

facts: A successful no-op is not progress. GLM can keep emitting the same to-do list (even while acknowledging the loop in prose) until the general step budget is exhausted. Give it a chance to recover, then fail explicitly.

Count identical completed to-do calls at the tail of this user turn. Prose/reasoning and per-step scaffolding are not progress. A different list, another tool, or a user message is. Only matched, completed calls count, so interrupted/failed tool execution cannot masquerade as this model loop.
Compare task/status rather than object key order or provider call IDs.
entries.title: Agent Runtime update: run-agent-step

ai.title: Stop agent runs stuck repeating an unchanged to-do list
ai.summary: The agent runtime now detects when an assistant emits the same completed `write_todos` list repeatedly without any other tool use. When the tail of `agentState.messageHistory` contains three identical completed calls, a tagged recovery message is injected; at six, `TodoLoopError` is thrown and surfaced as a failed turn, preventing budget exhaustion on models like GLM that loop silently. The comparison keys on the task/status pair rather than object key order or provider call IDs, and only matched, completed calls are counted so interrupted or failed tool execution cannot masquerade as progress.
ai.evidence: New file `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/todo-loop.ts` defines `trailingIdenticalTodoCalls`, `TodoLoopError`, and thresholds `TODO_LOOP_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD` (3) and `TODO_LOOP_STOP_THRESHOLD` (6); `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` calls `trailingIdenticalTodoCalls(agentState.messageHistory)` after tool results and throws `TodoLoopError` when consecutive identical `write_todos` calls reach the stop threshold, otherwise injects a tagged recovery user message.
ai.migration: No migration is required; existing runs that were already looping will now terminate, and users may retry with a different model or reasoning level after the stop message appears.
